name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Walkinshaw with $2.8M raised and heavy outside support
Republican Purves raised only ~$11K with $200 on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean, Walkinshaw's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty all point the same direction, so the forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied Safe D margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a major scandal would be the main reason to revisit, though nothing in the evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District leans heavily Democratic, and first-term incumbent James Walkinshaw is running for a full term with a large war chest. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, with substantial outside spending in his corner. Republican Arthur Purves has raised roughly $11,000 and reports only $200 in cash, giving him little capacity to compete. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the lopsided money gap, and prediction markets that price a Democratic win at about 98 percent. The expected margin is roughly 25 points, with the seat rated Safe Democratic.
